govdesc.Aigl Chormana: The Aigl who turned inland from the coasts became something different - opportunistic warlords who built confederations through pragmatism rather than tradition. These Chormana measure a ruler by successful raids and cunning tactics, not bloodlines or static domains. When an Aigl chieftain wishes to expand their warband, they call upon warriors across the open country, offering glory and plunder rather than gold.
govdesc.Central Chormana: In the harshest deserts and highest mountains, the Central Chormana wander as living defenders of sacred ground. Their Tatia leaders gather warriors not through gold but through shared faith and the promise of holy glory. When the call goes out, devout fighters across the badlands answer - drawn by ideology and the fame that comes from defending the faithful. These wandering hosts know every canyon and dune, making them nearly impossible to dislodge from prepared positions.
govdesc.Chormana Otija: The riders of legendary Otij mounts maintain their independence through bonds of mutual gain with the mountain Xacra. When an Otija khan raises their standard, mounted warriors answer from across the eastern wastes - drawn by the promise of glory and the reputation that comes from serving beside the finest cavalry in the region. These are not mercenaries bought with coin, but alliances forged through fame and shared pride in their ride. The Xacra provide support not as masters to servants, but as partners who recognize the value of swift riders.
govdesc.Western Chormana: The Qormaic tribes of the western hills transformed nomadic confederation into something resembling aristocracy - yet remained fundamentally Chormana. Their leaders attract elite warriors not with wages but through bonds of personal trust and the renown that comes from fighting beside the finest warriors in the region. Through careful selection and rigorous training traditions, they forge tight-knit brotherhoods where loyalty flows from mutual respect rather than feudal obligation.
govdesc.Eniol Supremacy: The Eniol Supremacy represents the warrior path, where martial prowess and aggressive expansion define legitimacy. Local lords rule provinces as their own fiefs, maintaining power through military strength and the cultivation of elite warriors. Though lacking influence, noble family house heads retain their family manor and pursue house aspiration through conquest and valor. Vassals operate with significant autonomy, building personal power bases and knight retinues.
govdesc.Eniol Mandate: The Eniol Mandate upholds traditional order through authoritarian control and the systematic enforcement of hierarchy. Local lords govern provinces with iron discipline, using surveillance, intimidation, and strict law enforcement to maintain stability. Though lacking influence, noble family house heads retain their family manor and pursue house aspiration through the accumulation of prestige and the demonstration of absolute authority. Vassals rule their domains with tight control, extracting maximum taxation while crushing dissent before it spreads.
govdesc.Eniol Administration: The Eniol Administration embodies the diplomatic path of centralized governance, where harmony and consensus guide the realm. Characters are appointed as governors based on their ability to maintain social cohesion and navigate complex political relationships. Administrators have access to influence, and noble family house heads maintain family manor estates and pursue house aspiration through refined statecraft.
govdesc.Eniol Technocracy: The Eniol Technocracy represents the scholarly path of governance, where knowledge and innovation drive progress toward an enlightened future. Characters are appointed as governors based on learning and technical expertise. Administrators have access to influence, and noble family house heads maintain family manor estates and pursue house aspiration through research and advancement. Vassals generally govern single counties, focusing on education, infrastructure, and technological development over military might.
govdesc.HuakKenVah: Under the HuakKenVah system, the jungle's harsh law becomes divine mandate. The HuakKen - supreme warrior-priest - rules through absolute military authority sanctified by the divine. From temple fortresses deep in unforgiving jungle, elite guards enforce the HuakKenVah: holy law delivered through disciplined force, where martial prowess proves spiritual worth and weakness is heresy. The weak are cast aside as the jungle demands, while the strong ascend to serve the HuakKen's sacred military order.
govdesc.Great Irchmo: The Great Irchmo serves as the spiritual and cultural center of the Floicht people, maintaining tributary networks through religious authority rather than military force. Temple administrators coordinate wide federations through spiritual influence, deal easily with peoples of other cultures, and hire mercenaries cheaply when persuasion fails. Its houses of healing leave its realms better protected against epidemics than their neighbours. It is hard to attack, and its levies are refilled quickly.
govdesc.Stormlander Rule: The Stormlanders are opportunistic coastal raiders who live by the sea and by what it carries. Their fleets are fast, safe in open water and quick to land an army, and they raid from their ships as a matter of course. Their strength on land is a small core of knights and hired regiments, paid for with prestige and plunder rather than taxes. Cunning and hardy, they respect proven warriors and scorn the weak. This way of life breeds friction at home.
govdesc.Blouck Tribal: The Blouck follow the law of the strong, where leadership is earned through proven strength and maintained through respect and fear. Like a pack, the strongest lead - but strength must be demonstrated through formalized frontal confrontation and ritual combat. Honor and prestige are paramount, earned through displays of physical prowess, courage in battle, and victory in ceremonial duels. Challengers may face the leader in sanctioned combat, with murder being an accepted outcome of these trials by strength.
govdesc.Broulqen Bureaucracy: The Broulqen Bureaucracy is a highly centralized government where power resides primarily within the imperial capital and its appointed administrators. Provincial governors are appointed to manage regional districts that combine civil governance with defense. These professionals collect taxes, administer justice, and command the district armies, creating an efficient state apparatus that balances bureaucratic control with military readiness. While birthright remains important, skill and loyalty matter more in the Broulqen system.
govdesc.Vieunn: The Vieunn - the Sail-people - are maritime warriors whose identity is inseparable from the waves they command. Whether ideological raiders redistributing wealth to the oppressed or pragmatic corsairs navigating neutrality, the Vieunn control island chains and coastal waters through unmatched naval prowess. Their fleets strike swiftly from the horizon, carrying warriors bred for mobility and raid warfare. The sea is not merely a path but their domain, their livelihood, and their legend.
govdesc.Malachite Mountain Empire: The Malachite Mountain Empire lives in vast cavern complexes beneath the peaks. Sheltered from the weather above, its underground cities make mountain and hill country prosper faster and yield more tax than surface dwellers manage, and its roads through that country are safe. Its fortresses are stronger and somewhat better garrisoned than others, and its armies fight with a marked advantage in mountains and hills. Life in the deep breeds careful stewards, scholars and schemers. The depths take their price.
govdesc.Knight Circles: The Knight Circles organize their realms around warrior brotherhoods, where prowess earns respect and position. Under a recognized Knight-Commander a circle is a household of sworn knights more than a state. Its members stand by their kin and by those who share their faith, and devotion is held to sharpen a commander's judgment in war. A circle venerates its strongest fighters and keeps one knight more than custom allows elsewhere. The standing of the circles lets them raise men at arms regiments with prestige instead of gold.
govdesc.Tribal Wanderers: The Thramptith Wanderers are free tribes that answer to no fixed seat. Some follow their herds, some follow the water, and a clan may do both in one lifetime. They move faster than settled peoples, graze lightly so the land recovers behind them, and are received without hostility by strangers of other faiths and cultures, with whom they deal easily. Their devotions travel with them. Freedom has its cost. A wandering clan builds little, so its lands prosper slowly.
govdesc.Meritocratic Forum: The Meritocratic Forum is a commonwealth in which power is earned through demonstrated competence and is never inherited. Its members advance by examination and proven work, and rank and reward follow the measured worth of a person to the whole. Governors are appointed for skill and learning, and the heads of the noble houses keep their estates and a voice in the Forum.
govdesc.Family Clans: The Family Clans organize their societies around extended family networks, with clan elders maintaining authority through consensus and family honor. Coastal, riverine, and inland clans cooperate through kinship bonds while maintaining strong family autonomy.

lore.title: Observer analysis: the Aiexqelt and the Aigl
lore.text: Linguistic survey, filed after Planetary Survey AK-7249. Two languages of the south-west were chosen for close study because each has shaped the politics of its speakers: Aiexqelt, the language of the Eniol empire, and Aigl, the language of the Stormlands.
sections: Aiexqelt: sounds

Consonants may be doubled, and doubling is meaningful. A doubled m marks a word that touches secrecy, oaths or hidden knowledge: mmalkæi, secret, mmaigol, the ritual silence, mmalvælt, curse, and mmolgoi, never. The hard x runs through the vocabulary of administration. Careful speech gives every vowel its full value, while casual speech wears them down to a neutral murmur, so the same sentence can be heard twice, once as a statement and once as a rumour. Names follow rank. An opening Mm- signals high status, Gl- nobility and Fl- the clerical class.
Aiexqelt: grammar

Words are built by adding endings, with seven cases. Formal speech puts the verb last, casual speech puts it in the middle, and the choice itself tells the listener how to take what is said. Verbs carry four levels of honour, from common to imperial, and must also state how the speaker knows a thing: seen, heard from another, or inferred. A witness in an Eniol court cannot give evidence without declaring its source in the grammar.
Aiexqelt: writing and law

The script is an abjad. Consonants are set in orderly square blocks of four, two down one column and two down the next, with space between blocks, and are always written. Vowels are added as marks in coloured ink and may be given in full, in part or not at all. One written skeleton can then be voiced as "king", "to rule", "kingdom" or "royal decree". This is used on purpose. Court and legal texts are fully marked to prevent dispute, private letters are half marked, and secret messages are left bare so that both parties can later claim another reading. To write the emperor's name without all its vowels is treason. To read a deliberate ambiguity the wrong way is a social disgrace. The most valued skill of an Eniol lawyer is a contract that holds two meanings, and the highest form of their poetry does the same thing for pleasure. Since the empire broke into four kingdoms, four dialects have begun to drift apart, and each faction now marks its vowels in its own shape. Dots and circles are the classical form, kept by the conservative faction that once ruled the whole.
Aigl: sounds

Aigl is carried by its vowels. Long runs of two and three vowels are common, words open with gl- or bl- and with no other cluster, and stress falls on the syllable before the last unless the speaker shifts it for effect in ritual speech.
Aigl: grammar

Words barely change form. Verbs do not mark person or number, and meaning is steered by small particles. Four of them grade belief: ia for what may be so, ee for what is certain, ai for what is doubted, and glo for what was revealed. Speakers also separate what they lived through from what came in a vision. The closing line of a common prophecy shows the habit: "Dimae ia, belaim ia", death maybe, life maybe. The Aigl treat this as plain accuracy.
Aigl: writing and rule

The script is cut into shell, bone and boat timber. It is an alphabet of rounded letters, one for each sound, written in a line from left to right. Optional marks for moon phase, wind, spirit and prophecy are added around the letters. Reading and writing count as attainment. Rulers are chosen for demonstrated learning, the test is the reading of old prophecies, and women are literate more often than men. A prophecy must be written before it may be spoken, and destroying a personal book of signs is among the gravest offences. What the Aigl call witchcraft contains no magic that this survey could detect. It is herb lore, weather lore and a sharp understanding of other people.
Assessment

Both languages make the speaker state how a thing is known. The Eniol use this to assign liability, and the Aigl use it to rank certainty. Neither people will be easy to deceive, and neither will be easy to convince. Anything an observer says to an Aiexqelt speaker will be recorded as hearsay with a named source. Anything said to an Aigl speaker will be answered with ia. Continued observation at a distance is recommended.

lore.title: The Words of the HuakKen
lore.text: The time of reckoning draws near, when all shall bend knee before the true faith or face divine judgment. Our ancestors paid in blood for these sacred truths, and we honor their sacrifice with our devotion. The unfaithful cry persecution, but know this - it is mercy to cleanse the impure, to burn away the rot that threatens to poison all of Thekan. Let the smoke of our sacred fires rise to the twin moons themselves, let the screams of heretics be a warning to those who would stray from righteousness. The Inner Sea itself bears witness to our holy purpose - its waters run deep with the blood of martyrs and the ashes of those who dared stand against divine will. When the final festival bells toll, when the last torch is lit, all shall know the price of defiance against the true path.

lore.title: The Chronicle of Miocched of Oumbor
lore.text: In the Year of the Twin Moons' Eclipse, when the waters of the Inner Sea ran red with the blood of a thousand ships, I, Miocched, Chief Chronicler of the Great Library of Oumbor, set forth to record the tumult that grips our sacred lands. From the frost-crowned peaks of Northern Thekan to the sun-scorched shores of the Southern realms, our world trembles with the footfalls of armies. The ancient prophecies speak true - when the Moons align in opposition, the peoples of Upper and Lower Thekan shall rise against one another, each claiming divine mandate over these blessed shores.

lore.title: The Treatise of Scholar Gouelde of Aikeq
lore.text: Let it be known to all who seek wisdom that I, Gouelde of the Ancient House of Aikeq, having studied the chronicles of a hundred generations, do hereby present my findings on the nature of our world. The great continent of Thekan, split by divine providence into its Upper and Lower realms by the Sacred Inner Sea, stands as a testament to the delicate balance of creation. In the North, where the Chorwangorm holds dominion over ancient territories, to the South where the princes of Xoflour and Lidru vie for supremacy - all are bound by ties of trade, blood, and ancient enmity.

lore.title: Planetary Survey Report AK-7249
lore.text: Initial analysis reveals a medieval civilization spanning the continental mass designated "Thekan." The planet's binary lunar system has shaped maritime development and cultural practices across two distinct regions divided by an inland sea. Settlement patterns suggest a feudal society with fortified positions at strategic elevations and waterways. Continued observation recommended to document the unique evolutionary path of this civilization under twin lunar influence.
